intro: Great progress! Now we put words together into real sentences. You'll practise English word order (Subject + Verb + Object), using 'a' and 'an', and making plurals like books and boxes. Warm-up: try one short sentence about what you like — for example, 'I like coffee.'
teachingNotes: Word order is usually the same as Indonesian (S-V-O), which helps; stress that English almost always needs a subject (no 'Like coffee').
Indonesian has no articles: learners drop 'a/an'. 'an' goes before vowel SOUNDS (an apple, an hour, a university).
Indonesian plurals repeat the word (buku-buku); English adds -s/-es. After numbers, English still needs -s (two books).
Use only simple present with I/you/we/they to avoid third-person -s (that comes in A1).

keyPoints.title: Subject + Verb + Object
keyPoints.explanation: Most English sentences start with who does the action, then the action, then the thing. Always include the subject.

keyPoints.title: a or an
keyPoints.explanation: Use a/an before one countable thing. Use 'an' before a vowel sound (an apple, an egg), 'a' before a consonant sound (a book, a car).

keyPoints.title: Plurals with -s / -es
keyPoints.explanation: Add -s for more than one: book → books. Add -es after s, x, ch, sh: box → boxes, watch → watches. Don't repeat the word like in Indonesian.

blocks.text: Most English sentences follow the same order: **who** (subject) → **does what** (verb) → **to what** (object). Unlike Indonesian, you can't drop the subject: *Makan nasi* must be **I eat rice**.

id.text: Sebagian besar kalimat bahasa Inggris mengikuti urutan yang sama: **siapa** (subjek) → **melakukan apa** (kata kerja) → **terhadap apa** (objek). Berbeda dari bahasa Indonesia, subjek tidak boleh dihilangkan: *Makan nasi* harus menjadi **I eat rice**.

blocks.text: Use **a** or **an** before **one** countable thing when you first mention it. The choice depends on the **sound**, not the letter: **an** before a vowel sound (*an apple, an hour*), **a** before a consonant sound (*a book, a university*).

id.text: Gunakan **a** atau **an** sebelum **satu** benda yang bisa dihitung saat pertama disebut. Pilihannya bergantung pada **bunyi**, bukan huruf: **an** sebelum bunyi vokal (*an apple, an hour*), **a** sebelum bunyi konsonan (*a book, a university*).

blocks.explain: Egg starts with a vowel sound, so an egg.

id.explain: Egg diawali bunyi vokal, jadi an egg.

blocks.text: For more than one, add **-s**: *book → books*. Add **-es** after s, x, ch and sh: *box → boxes, watch → watches*. Don't repeat the word like Indonesian *buku-buku*, and keep the -s even after a number: **two books**.

id.text: Untuk lebih dari satu, tambahkan **-s**: *book → books*. Tambahkan **-es** setelah s, x, ch dan sh: *box → boxes, watch → watches*. Jangan mengulang kata seperti *buku-buku*, dan walaupun sudah ada angka, -s tetap dipakai: **two books**.

blocks.explain: Bus ends in s, so add -es: buses.

id.explain: Bus berakhiran s, jadi tambah -es: buses.

blocks.text: Short, complete sentences are what you need for messages and forms: *I need a room. We have two bags. She is an engineer.* Check three things: a subject, a verb, and a/an or -s on the noun.

id.text: Kalimat pendek yang lengkap adalah yang kamu butuhkan untuk pesan dan formulir: *I need a room. We have two bags. She is an engineer.* Cek tiga hal: ada subjek, ada kata kerja, dan a/an atau -s pada kata benda.

blocks.text: Read your sentence and ask: who? does what? one or many?

id.text: Baca kalimatmu dan tanyakan: siapa? melakukan apa? satu atau banyak?

suggestedQuestions: Why do I always need a subject?
When do I add -es instead of -s?
Why don't we say 'buku-buku' in English?

id.intro: Kemajuan yang bagus! Sekarang kita susun kata menjadi kalimat sungguhan. Kamu akan berlatih urutan kata bahasa Inggris (Subjek + Kata Kerja + Objek), memakai 'a' dan 'an', dan membuat bentuk jamak seperti books dan boxes. Pemanasan: coba buat satu kalimat pendek tentang sesuatu yang kamu suka — misalnya 'I like coffee.'
